findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: A generic `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). Not found or access denied should be a `TRPCError` with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. Otherwise the error is logged and reported as a server fault, and clients cannot distinguish it from a real failure.

findings.title: Delegation credentials can get the delete-cache action, but the handler rejects them
findings.body: `hasCache` only checks the Google type and `cacheUpdatedAt`. Delegation credentials have in-memory negative IDs and are not in the Credential table. The server handler looks up `credential.findFirst({ userId })` and will throw for them. The UI can offer an action that always fails with a generic error toast.

findings.title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: The handler constructs the real `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of using the `CalendarCache.init` factory. That factory returns the mock when caching is disabled. The status query therefore always hits the DB. It also reports stale cache rows even when the feature is off. Delegation credentials have negative IDs and will never match any rows.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data does not bump updatedAt reliably
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(id, {})` sends an empty data object. Prisma may skip the update, or may not apply `@updatedAt`, so the call can be a no-op. It also touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each cache refresh, which adds write load for no displayed benefit (the PR notes the UI doesn't use it).

findings.title: macOS-only sed -i syntax in a committed script
findings.body: `sed -i ''` works only with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU/Linux it treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env file is not updated. The script is also unrelated to this feature and has no documentation.

findings.title: Hard-coded en-US date formatting
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with a fixed "en-US" locale instead of the user's locale, so non-English users see US-style dates.
